analysis_trace: Trial NCT06742515 is a Phase 2, single-arm study evaluating blinatumomab plus reduced-dose chemotherapy (including venetoclax in cycle 2) in newly diagnosed Ph-negative precursor B-ALL patients aged 15-59 years. Primary endpoint is CR with negative MRD by flow cytometry after cycles 1 and 2.

Evidence from NCT05557110 (ASH 2023 abstract) shows reduced-dose chemotherapy followed by blinatumomab achieved 100% CR/CRi rate and 95.5% MRD negativity in 21 evaluable newly diagnosed Ph-negative B-ALL adults. This provides direct evidence for similar patient population and treatment approach.

Evidence from blinatumomab-venetoclax combination studies (GMALL BLIVEN phase 1/2) in relapsed/refractory or MRD-positive B-ALL shows CR rates of 44-100% depending on setting, with MRD negativity achievable. Venetoclax adds BCL-2 inhibition synergy.
E1910 trial (NEJM 2024) demonstrated blinatumomab added to consolidation improved 3-year OS from 68% to 85% in MRD-negative adults, establishing blinatumomab's survival benefit.
Meta-analysis of upfront blinatumomab in adolescents/adults with Ph-negative B-ALL showed pooled CR rate 77% (95% CI 70-83%) for induction use and pooled 3-year OS 67% (55-78%).

Key uncertainties: NCT06742515 includes venetoclax in cycle 2 which differs from NCT05557110; small sample size (n=20); no direct published results for this specific regimen; EFS/OS data immature in similar trials.

Evidence roles: NCT05557110 results = direct_numeric for CR/MRD endpoints; E1910 = indirect_direction for OS; meta-analysis = indirect_direction for ranges; venetoclax combination data = mechanism_background supporting enhanced efficacy.
Safety considerations: blinatumomab-associated CRS (grade 1-3) and neurotoxicity are manageable; venetoclax adds infection risk; reduced-dose chemotherapy lowers toxicity vs hyper-CVAD.
